scope: Post-release Tracker-Android consumer smoke for the immutable Tracebox 0.1.0-alpha.5 package.

checks.evidence: The launcher activity completed a cold start twice; the initial launch completed in 4271 ms and the restart completed in 2537 ms. No FATAL EXCEPTION entry was observed.
The application and private com.adsamcik.tracker.debug:tracebox_handler processes were simultaneously live under the same application UID after both cold starts.
Android loaded libtracebox_crashpad.so from the installed alpha.5 APK's x86_64 library directory in both the application and handler processes.

requested-policy-v2, requested-profile-v1, policy-control-v1, and identity-lifecycle-v1 existed under the Tracebox no-backup owned root before and after force-stop/cold restart; the diagnostics UI reported Readiness: durable and Health: ready after restart.

The marked no_backup/tracebox root contained bounded policy, identity, UID-quota, segment, raw-journal, native emergency, Rust panic, and handler-client state. No contents or Tracker user data were read.
The Tracker Settings screen exposed the localized Crash diagnostics entry and opened Tracebox's localized diagnostics screen.
Review disclosed one diagnostic item and 109 exact bytes, stated that raw crash artifacts were excluded and privacy transformations were applied, and required explicit APPROVE AND CONTINUE.
Approval opened Android's system chooser for one .tbdiag file. The Tracker screen exposed share and save actions and no upload action or endpoint.
The approved .tbdiag existed only in Tracebox export staging while the diagnostics screen retained the approved package; navigating away removed every staged .tbdiag match.
